clue.text: Tin-opener is breaking into the drink, that's obvious

indicators.note: the opener of tin is its first letter, the one that starts the word
one piece breaking into another forces its way inside it

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a typical drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone opening a tin of drink states the plainly evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget, but it means the first letter of 'Tin'. 'breaking into' puts IS inside RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident statement, too obvious to need saying, is a platitude of this kind.

clue.text: Light working in material manufacture

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Light is being used in the making of a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial textile fibre made from cellulose, a manufactured fabric.

clue.text: Bring in present

explanation.surface: Bring in a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something new is to bring it in; to make one person known to another formally is to present them.

clue.text: Grass whichever way you look

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so it looks alike from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Grass is all around, wherever you turn your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: MARRAM is a palindrome; the clue's second half is the only wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse seaside dune grass used to bind sand.

clue.text: This struggle of course may have involved Jutes

definitions.text: This struggle of course may have involved Jutes

parts.words: This struggle of course may have involved Jutes
parts.note: reads as a historical battle with the Jutes, the Germanic invaders of England; really a school sports-day race run in sacks made of jute fibre

explanation.surface: A conflict that naturally involved the Jutes, the tribe that settled in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' hides a racecourse; 'Jutes' looks like the tribe but means sacks of jute, the coarse fibre used for sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's contest where runners hop along inside bags is run in hessian sacks woven from jute.

clue.text: An old order on the way liable to be costly

definitions.text: An old order on the way liable to be costly

parts.words: An old order on the way liable to be costly
parts.note: an old command given on the highway that costs the hearer dearly: the demand of a highwayman robbing travellers

explanation.surface: A command from the past, given on the road, that may cost the listener a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is a command, not a sequence, and 'the way' is the highway where robbers held up coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the traditional demand of mounted robbers holding up coaches, telling travellers to halt and hand over valuables.

clue.text: End to contest when short left jabbed in

indicators.note: a letter jabbed in is pushed inside another word

parts.note: to contest is to compete
L is the short form, the abbreviation, of left

explanation.surface: A boxing bout ends as a quick left jab lands.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a task is to complete it, bringing it to its end.

clue.text: Flier who departed after a little quarrel

annotationWithheld.clue: Flier who departed after a little quarrel

clue.text: Crate in no order to provide a receptacle

indicators.note: putting letters in order rearranges them, so these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A crate, disordered, serves as a box to hold things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in no order' looks like a phrase about chaos; 'order' is the anagram signal and 'in no' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any box, tin or vessel for holding things.

clue.text: Marine establishment promoting native developments

parts.note: reads as a naval base backing local projects; natives are oysters bred in British waters, and this seabed business rears them

explanation.surface: A naval base encourages progress among the local population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native' is the trade name for a British-bred oyster, such as the Whitstable native.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a coastal business where shellfish are cultivated in beds until ready for market.

clue.text: A dishonest inclination

explanation.surface: A crooked tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt officials are called crooked or bent in British slang; a natural tendency or talent is a bent.

clue.text: Unfavourable review drawn out

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again, here reworking the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A bad critique that drags on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means inconvenient or adverse, so it is a synonym for unfortunate in this sense.

clue.text: Come ashore with gold to transport

parts.note: to come ashore is to land
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Arrive on the coast bringing gold to carry away.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle of the past.

clue.text: Banned cricketer retiring you say?

indicators.note: a cricketer retiring goes back to the pavilion, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: 'say' asks for what is spoken: the letter U is pronounced like the word given

parts.note: the word whose sound gives the letter

explanation.surface: A batsman who has been banned is walking off, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns BAT round to TAB; 'say' tells you the letter U sounds like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, something forbidden by custom.

clue.text: Pay attention to social worker's assistant

parts.note: to attend is to pay attention to
the ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: Listen to the social worker's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a council job but is the crossword's favourite insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is a helper or servant who waits on someone.

clue.text: Teachers require payment to admit one for feeding

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British union

indicators.note: a word admitting another lets it in, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Teachers demand payment before letting someone in for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used for feeding provides nourishment to a living thing.

clue.text: Charge journalist about article, it is suggested

indicators.note: the charge and journalist go about, around, the article

parts.note: to indict is to formally charge with a crime
a is the indefinite article
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Bring charges against a reporter over a piece he wrote, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside INDICTED, the charge and journalist together.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point to it or hint at it, much as to suggest it.

clue.text: Prison enclosure showing signs of disturbance

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
a ring is an enclosure, as in a boxing ring or circus ring

explanation.surface: A prison yard shows signs of unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stirring is beginning to move or become agitated, waking into activity.

clue.text: A troop leader put on trial for having sworn

indicators.note: the leader of the word troop is its first letter

parts.note: something put on trial has been tested

explanation.surface: A soldier's commander was tried for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn statement is one formally vouched for, given under oath as evidence.

clue.text: Soviet agreement to Navy repair

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The Russians agree to let the fleet fix things.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn is to mend a hole in fabric by weaving thread across it.

clue.text: Criticises strikes

explanation.surface: Faults hits.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something is to run it down with criticism; it is also to hit or rap something.

clue.text: Tether to bed with sheet perhaps

explanation.surface: Tie someone to a bed with a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks domestic, but 'bed' is the seabed and 'sheet' is the sheet anchor, a large ship's anchor for emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's heavy hook holds it to the seabed; the sheet anchor is one such hook, kept for emergencies.

clue.text: A prophet some chose as leader

indicators.note: some of these words gives a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Some picked a prophet as their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Creature found on the sidewalk?

parts.note: an American pavement animal, read instead as one that walks sideways on dry ground

explanation.surface: An animal seen on an American pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sidewalk' is not the pavement but a sideways walk, the gait of a crab, here one living on land.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crustacean that lives mainly on land, scuttling sideways like its sea relatives.

clue.text: Fuss about love

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Make a fuss about love.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to worship or cherish them deeply.

clue.text: This could be said from the platform

definitions.text: This could be said from the platform

parts.words: This could be said from the platform
parts.note: seems to be a speech given from a stage; it is the stage itself, the raised floor that a speech is given from

explanation.surface: A speaker announces something from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is not a remark but the platform itself, the thing one speaks from.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at the end of a hall for speakers or dignitaries.

clue.text: The appeal of a trendy career

parts.note: something in is fashionable or trendy
a vocation is a calling or career

explanation.surface: Why a fashionable job is so attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' looks like attraction but is an entreaty or prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An invocation is a prayer or entreaty calling on a higher power for help.

clue.text: Less familiar foreign: monarch

parts.note: strange means foreign or alien
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A foreign king is less well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something less known is more unfamiliar, an outsider.

clue.text: Southern summer is more miserable

parts.note: a summer here is one who sums, an adder of figures

explanation.surface: A southern summer is gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadder is the comparative of sad, meaning more unhappy.
